public_rationale: There is material counterevidence: a survey public before the post reported improving AI-product margins in 2025. But it covers software companies building AI products and does not isolate named startups or their whole-company margins. The relevant named-company reports were inaccessible or explicitly partial. I would not support the universal assertion, but these admissible records do not meet the stricter company-and-metric test for a definitive contradiction.
limitations: The two cited items describe the same survey.
The 2026 margin projection is not treated as an achieved result.
Failure to verify an accessible counterexample does not establish that no counterexample exists.

statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

from_speaker: nobody’s margins appear to be improving
None of them are improving their margins
our_interpretation: Read this as a factual claim about observable margin trends at AI startups. The repeated unqualified wording in the context makes it stronger than a statement of personal uncertainty.
Gross margin is the ordinary reading in this discussion of model-serving costs. It is distinct from operating margin, net margin and profitability.
Use the latest completed calendar year, 2025, compared with the preceding year, plus pre-post reporting about that period. This is an evaluator-selected period for the ongoing observation.
The context relies on private-company financial reporting, so the intended basis is estimated margins rather than an explicitly stated GAAP or IFRS measure.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable reported gross-margin trends establish no improvement across the relevant AI-startup population.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one identifiable AI startup has a credible, comparable gross-margin increase in the target period. Becoming profitable is not required.
